title: Small healthcare practices: HIPAA Security Rule risk analysis and documentation burden is asserted low by HHS but unmeasured

history.reason: Signal from HHS/OCR January 2025 NPRM small-entity and cost analysis.
NPRM and Unified Agenda entry read; HHS cost, small-entity and status statements recorded with counterevidence. Burden on small practices remains unmeasured; rule not final.

description: HIPAA covered entities, most of them small, must already perform a thorough risk analysis and document Security Rule compliance. HHS proposed in January 2025 to add a written asset inventory and network map, annual compliance audits and more written policies. HHS estimates about $1,235 per entity per year and certifies no significant small-entity impact; the actual time and cost for small practices are not measured in the sources read.
customer_segment: Small HIPAA covered entities (HHS counts about 740,348 small covered entities, 90 percent of 822,609), including small medical and mental health practices; business associates also affected.
context: The rule is only a proposal (NPRM 90 FR 898, January 6, 2025). The latest Unified Agenda edition read lists it as a Long-Term Action with final action projected July 2027; no final rule was found in a Federal Register search on 2026-11-04. Existing requirements (risk analysis, documentation) apply today regardless.

evidence.text: HHS states regulated entities are already required to conduct an accurate and thorough risk analysis, including an inventory of technology assets and mapping ePHI movement.

HHS estimates 740,348 small covered entities (90 percent of 822,609) and an annualized cost of about $1,235 per regulated entity, and proposes to certify no significant economic effect on a substantial number of small entities.
HHS estimates first-year costs of about $9 billion and about $6 billion per year thereafter across regulated entities and plan sponsors.
HHS cites NCVHS testimony of a widespread lack of robust risk analysis among covered entities and business associates, indicating that documentation of the existing duty is often absent or weak.
The Unified Agenda entry (pubId 202510) lists the rule as a Long-Term Action with final action projected 07/00/2027; the Spring 2025 edition had projected 05/00/2026.
Small practices without in-house security staff may spend significant owner or office-manager time, or outside fees, producing and maintaining risk analysis and written documentation.

alternatives: Outsourced IT and managed service providers, compliance consultants and HIPAA compliance software: not investigated.
Free HHS/ONC security risk assessment tooling: existence and use by small practices not verified in the sources read.

contradictory_evidence.text: HHS, the rule-writer, estimates about $1,235 per entity per year and says small entities bear lower cost per establishment; this is an ex ante agency estimate, not measured burden.

HHS costs the compliance audit at about 2 hours per entity on the assumption that compliance activities are already documented; where documentation is missing, the cost is understated, and HHS lists asset inventory and documentation of existing requirements as not readily quantified.
The rule is a proposal that has slipped from a projected 2026 to 2027 final action, so the incremental requirements may never take effect in this form.
Software and hosting vendors may absorb much of the work for the smallest firms (HHS assumption); vendor coverage is unknown.

uncertainty: Unknown: actual hours and fees small practices spend on risk analysis and documentation today; what share lack a current written risk analysis; how many already use paid tools or consultants; comment-letter positions of physician and small-practice groups; whether and in what form the rule is finalized; the Spring 2026 Unified Agenda status.
open_questions: What do small practices actually spend (time and fees) on risk analysis and Security Rule documentation?
What share of small practices have a current, written risk analysis (OCR enforcement data, independent surveys)?
What do public comments from small-practice groups say about the NPRM burden estimates?
What do existing HIPAA compliance tools and consultants cost, and where do they fall short?
next_actions: Read OCR enforcement actions and published settlements for risk analysis failures at small entities.
Read public comment letters from physician and small-practice associations on regulations.gov docket HHS-OCR-0945-AA22.
Find an independent survey of small-practice HIPAA compliance time and spend.
Re-check rule status via the Spring 2026 Unified Agenda before further work.
